stops.title: Winterlandschap met ijsvermaak
stops.story_quote: He adapted compositional elements reminiscent of Pieter Bruegel, whose expansive crowd scenes Avercamp reinterpreted
specifics_traced: Avercamp, c.1608, oil on oak panel, ~23 years old (documented, consistent with his 1585 birth year)
style recalls Bruegel's 1565 Winter Landscape (confirmed, Wikipedia)

stops.title: Gezicht op huizen in Delft ('The Little Street')
stops.story_quote: A 1696 auction catalogue records 'The Little House' as one of at least three cityscapes by Vermeer
specifics_traced: Vermeer, c.1658, painted from his own window (documented)
1696 Amsterdam sale catalogue listing (confirmed, WGA provenance)
one of only ~2-3 known Vermeer cityscapes (confirmed)

stops.title: De bedreigde zwaan (The Threatened Swan)
stops.story_quote: Later, the museum's director Van de Weyer insisted on displaying the painting prominently
specifics_traced: later read as political allegory re: Dutch sovereignty (confirmed)

fabrications.claim: a museum 'director Van de Weyer' insisted on displaying it prominently
fabrications.why: no such Rijksmuseum director found in the historical record (the documented first-purchase decision was by Cornelis Sebille Roos/Alexander Gogel for the Nationale Kunst-Galerij, not a 'Van de Weyer'); appears invented

stops.title: Het melkmeisje (The Milkmaid)
stops.story_quote: Because of a debate, the government decided to buy the work for the Rijksmuseum. As a result, 'The Milkmaid' remained in the Netherlands
specifics_traced: Dutch government controversially purchased it in 1908 to keep it from leaving the country (broadly consistent with documented history)

stops.title: De grote golf bij Kanagawa (The Great Wave)
stops.story_quote: The delicate gradations of Prussian blue pigment, first synthesized in Germany and imported from Europe
specifics_traced: Prussian blue pigment imported to Japan via Europe/China (documented art-historical fact)

stops.title: A Militiaman Holding a Berkemeyer
stops.story_quote: This work reflects a turning point in his career, where he moved beyond formal group portraits to capture individuals

defects: far fewer D511 stories than the other Rijksmuseum text (1 vs 3) despite similar factual accuracy — mostly description, not narrative
one_line_verdict: Accurate and well-sourced but mostly descriptive rather than story-driven; one invented curatorial anecdote.
